lesson.headline: JLPT N5 (Beginner) — Phonetics, Particles & 10 Core Kanji
lesson.lead: Establishing the foundational blocks of the Japanese language. Covers Hiragana, Katakana, crucial structural particles, and essential character definitions.
bullets: Hiragana & Katakana: Hiragana is utilized for native grammatical structures, while Katakana represents borrowed foreign terms (e.g. カメラ - kamera).
Structural Particles: は (wa - topic marker), の (no - possession), に (ni - time/destination), を (o - direct object), が (ga - subject marker).
Greetings & Aisatsu: こんにちは (Konnichiwa - Hello *written with は), ありがとう (Arigatou - Thank you).
N5 Core Kanji: 一 (ichi - one), 二 (ni - two), 三 (san - three), 人 (hito - person), 日 (hi - sun/day), 本 (hon - book/origin), 水 (mizu - water), 木 (ki - tree), 金 (kane - gold/money), 土 (tsuchi - soil).

quizzes.q: Choose the correct form to express permission: "May I eat this cake?" (このケーキを___もいいですか。)
quizzes.explain: The grammar pattern "~てもいいですか" (~te mo ii desu ka) is used to ask for permission. The Te-form of 食べる is 食べて.

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence to mean "Please do not open the window": "窓を___でください。"
quizzes.explain: The pattern "~ないでください" (~nai de kudasai) is used for polite negative requests ("please don't do X"). The Nai-form of 開ける is 開けない.

quizzes.q: How do you say "I want to watch a movie" in Japanese? (映画が___です。)
quizzes.explain: To express desire to do an action, replace the "~masu" ending of the verb stem with "~tai". 見ます (to watch) stem is 見, so it becomes 見たい (want to watch).

quizzes.q: Choose the correct connector to mean "while reading a book": "本を___がら、お茶を飲みます。"
quizzes.explain: The grammar pattern "~ながら" (~nagara) indicates doing two actions simultaneously. It attaches to the verb stem (Masu-stem). 読みます stem is 読み.

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "Yesterday, I watched a movie, did some shopping, and so on." (昨日は映画を見たり、買い物をご___りしました。)
quizzes.explain: The pattern "~たり ~たり する" (~tari ~tari suru) lists activities. It attaches to the Ta-form (past casual). The past casual of する is した, so it becomes したり.

quizzes.q: How do you say "I have been to Japan before"? (日本へ行った___があります。)
quizzes.explain: The pattern "Verb (Ta-form) + ことがあます" indicates past experience ("have done X before"). 行った is the Ta-form of 行く.

quizzes.q: Choose the correct phrase to express obligation: "I must study Japanese." (日本語を勉強しなければ___。)
quizzes.explain: The pattern "~なければなりません" (~nakereba narimasen) expresses strong obligation or necessity ("must do X").

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "Because it is hot, I will open the window." (暑い___、窓を開けます。)
quizzes.explain: The particle "から" (kara) is used to state a reason or cause ("because..."). It is added directly after adjectives and verbs.

quizzes.q: Choose the correct form for "Let's buy a coffee": "コーヒーを___ましょう。"
quizzes.explain: The polite invitation/suggestion form "~ましょう" (~mashou) is attached to the verb Masu-stem. 買います stem is 買い.

quizzes.q: How do you say "I am studying Japanese now" (ongoing action)? (今、日本語を勉強して___。)
quizzes.explain: The pattern "Te-form + います" (~te imasu) represents an ongoing progressive action or current state.

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence to mean "Please read this book": "この本を___ください。"
quizzes.explain: The pattern "Te-form + ください" (~te kudasai) is a polite request ("please do X"). The Te-form of 読む is 読んで.

quizzes.q: Choose the correct ending to mean "It became cold": "寒く___。"
quizzes.explain: To describe a change of state, use "~くなる" (~ku naru) for I-adjectives. 寒い becomes 寒く, and past tense of なる is なりました.

quizzes.q: How do you say "Tennis is more interesting than soccer"? (サッカーよりテニスのほうが___。)
quizzes.explain: The comparison structure "A より B のほうが [adjective]" means "B is more [adjective] than A".

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence to mean "I like dogs": "わたしは犬___好きです。"
quizzes.explain: The adjective 好き (suki - like/love) requires the object to be marked with the particle が (ga).

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence to mean "Before eating a meal, wash your hands": "ご飯を食べる___、手を洗います。"
quizzes.explain: The pattern "Verb (Dictionary form) + まえに" (mae ni) means "before doing X".

quizzes.q: Choose the correct verb conjugation for "I decided not to go": "行かないことに___。"
quizzes.explain: The grammar pattern "~ことにする" (~koto ni suru) means "to decide to do / not do X". Past tense is しました.

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "Please eat without putting sugar in": "砂糖を入れ___で食べてください。"
quizzes.explain: The pattern "Verb (Nai-form without -i) + ないで" (~nai de) means "without doing X". 入れ(る) negative is 入れない.

quizzes.q: Choose the correct expression for "It is easy to understand this book": "この本は分かり___です。"
quizzes.explain: The suffix "~やすい" (~yasui) attached to a Masu-stem means "easy to do". 分かります stem is 分かり, so it is 分かりやすい.

quizzes.q: Choose the correct expression for "It is difficult to write this Kanji": "この漢字は書き___です。"
quizzes.explain: The suffix "~にくい" (~nikui) attached to a Masu-stem means "difficult to do". 書きます stem is 書き, so it is 書きにくい.

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence to mean "I want a new car": "新しい車___欲しいです。"
quizzes.explain: The adjective 欲しい (hoshii - want/desire) takes the particle が (ga) to mark the desired object.

quizzes.q: What is the correct form to say "After taking a shower, I slept"? (シャワーを___から寝ました。)
quizzes.explain: The pattern "Te-form + から" (~te kara) means "after doing X". The Te-form of あびる (to take a shower) is あびて.

quizzes.q: Choose the correct ending to mean "I think she is nice": "彼女は優しいと___。"
quizzes.explain: The pattern "[Casual clause] + と思います" (~to omoimasu) means "I think that...".

quizzes.q: Choose the correct form for "Shall we go together?": "一緒に行き___か。"
quizzes.explain: The pattern "~ましょうか" (~mashou ka) is used to offer to do something or suggest an action ("shall we...").

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "This room is clean and beautiful." (この部屋はきれいで、___です。)
quizzes.explain: To connect a Na-adjective to another clause, use the "de" form (きれい + で). The final clause finishes with the standard adjective + です (明るいです).

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "Because it was raining, I did not go out." (雨が降っていた___、出かけませんでした。)
quizzes.explain: Both から and ので indicate reasons. "ので" (node) is slightly more polite, soft, and objective, making it a perfect match here.

quizzes.q: Choose the correct word: "I intend to go to Tokyo next week." (来週、東京へ行く___です。)
quizzes.explain: The pattern "Verb (Dictionary form) + つもりです" expresses intention or planning to do an action.

quizzes.q: How do you say "It is already 3 o'clock" in Japanese? (___３時です。)
quizzes.explain: "もう" (mou) means "already" or "now". "まだ" (mada) means "yet" or "still".

quizzes.q: How do you say "I don't understand Japanese yet" in Japanese? (日本語が___分かりません。)
quizzes.explain: Pair "まだ" (mada) with a negative verb to mean "not yet" ("I do not understand yet").

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "Please turn off the television." (テレビを___てください。)
quizzes.explain: The Te-form of 消す (kesu - to turn off/erase) is 消して (keshite).

quizzes.q: Choose the correct form to mean "You must not enter this room": "この部屋に入ってはいけ___。"
quizzes.explain: The pattern "~てはいけません" (~te wa ikemasen) indicates strong prohibition ("must not do X").

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "Please do it slowly." (___してください。)
quizzes.explain: "ゆっくり" (yukkuri) means "slowly" or "leisurely". "だんだん" means gradually.

quizzes.q: Choose the correct conjugation to mean "I did not study yesterday": "昨日は勉強___。"
quizzes.explain: The polite past negative of する is しませんでした.

quizzes.q: Choose the correct form to mean "Please write your name here": "ここに名前を___ください。"
quizzes.explain: The Te-form of 書く (kaku - to write) is 書いて (kaite).

quizzes.q: Choose the correct conjugation of "good" (いい) in the past tense: "The weather was good yesterday." (昨日は天気が___です。)
quizzes.explain: The irregular adjective いい (ii - good) is conjugated using its classical form よい (yoi). Its past tense is よかった.

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence to mean "Please read this in a quiet voice": "静かな声で___ください。"
quizzes.explain: The Te-form of 話す (hanasu - to speak/talk) is 話して (hanashite).

quizzes.q: Choose the correct form: "I will do my homework after returning home." (うちへ帰ってから、宿題を___。)
quizzes.explain: The sentence ends politely with します (shimasu - to do).

quizzes.q: Choose the correct word for "Please turn left at the next corner": "次の角を左に___てください。"
quizzes.explain: The Te-form of 曲がる (magaru - to turn) is 曲がって (magatte).

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "I went to buy food." (食べ物を買___に行きました。)
quizzes.explain: The pattern "Masu-stem + に行く" (ni iku) expresses the purpose of going. 買います stem is 買い.

quizzes.q: Choose the correct word: "My father is taller than my mother." (父は母より背が___です。)
quizzes.explain: "背が高い" (se ga takai) is the standard Japanese phrase for "tall" (of a person).

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "The library is quiet." (図書館は___です。)
quizzes.explain: Before です, Na-adjectives drop their trailing "na". So 静かな becomes 静か です.

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "I bought a cheap watch." (___時計を買いました。)
quizzes.explain: I-adjectives directly modify nouns in their plain dictionary form (安い + 時計).

quizzes.q: Choose the correct ending to mean "Let's rest a little": "少し休み___。"
quizzes.explain: "休む" (yasumu - to rest) becomes "休みましょう" (yasumimashou - let's rest) to suggest an action.

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence to mean "Please show me that photo": "その写真を見___てください。"
quizzes.explain: The verb is 見せる (miseru - to show). Its Te-form is 見せて (misete).

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence to mean "I came to meet my friend": "友達に会___に来ました。"
quizzes.explain: The purpose of coming is marked by "Masu-stem + に来ました". 会います stem is 会い.

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "This box is light." (この箱は___です。)
quizzes.explain: "軽い" (karui) means light (weight). "重い" (omoi) means heavy.

quizzes.q: Choose the correct word: "That building is very high." (あのビルはとても___です。)
quizzes.explain: "高い" (takai) means high or expensive. "低い" (hikui) means low.

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "This water is cold." (この水は___です。)
quizzes.explain: "冷たい" (tsumetai) is used for cold objects/liquids. "寒い" (samui) is used for cold atmospheric temperature/weather.

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "Today is a cold day." (今日は___日です。)
quizzes.explain: Use "寒い" (samui) to describe the cold weather/temperature of the day.

quizzes.q: Choose the correct word: "I bought three apples." (りんごを___買いました。)
quizzes.explain: The generic counter for round/general items is "~つ" (~tsu). ３つ (mittsu) is three.

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence to mean "Please wait for a moment": "少々お持ち___。"
quizzes.explain: The polite honorific request pattern is "お + Masu-stem + ください". "お待ちください" means "Please wait".

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "I drink coffee every morning." (毎朝コーヒー___飲みます。)
quizzes.explain: The particle "を" (o) marks the direct object of the transitive verb 飲みます (to drink).

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "I go to school by bicycle." (自転車___学校へ行きます。)
quizzes.explain: The particle "で" (de) marks the means or instrument of an action (by bicycle).

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "There is a teacher in the classroom." (教室___先生がいます。)
quizzes.explain: The particle "に" (ni) marks the location of existence for animate objects with the verb います.

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "I study at the library." (図書館___勉強します。)
quizzes.explain: The particle "で" (de) marks the location where an active event or action takes place.

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "I will go to Tokyo next week." (来週、東京___行きます。)
quizzes.explain: The particle "へ" (e) marks the direction or destination of motion verbs like 行きます (to go).

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "I bought a book and a pen." (本___ペンを買いました。)
quizzes.explain: The particle "と" (to) is used to exhaustively connect nouns ("and").

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "I bought a book and a pen, among other things." (本___ペンなどを買いました。)
quizzes.explain: The particle "や" (ya) is used for a non-exhaustive list of items ("X and Y, among others").

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "I also like oranges." (みかん___好きです。)
quizzes.explain: The particle "も" (mo) replaces は/が/を to mean "also" or "too".

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "This is my umbrella." (これはわたし___傘です。)
quizzes.explain: The particle "の" (no) connects two nouns to show possession ("my umbrella").

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "I went to the department store with my friend." (友達___デパートへ行きました。)
quizzes.explain: The particle "と" (to) marks the companion with whom you do an action ("with").

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "Yesterday, I slept at 10 o'clock." (昨日は１０時___寝ました。)
quizzes.explain: The particle "に" (ni) marks a specific numerical point in time.

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "I study from Monday to Friday." (月曜日___金曜日まで勉強します。)
quizzes.explain: The particle "から" (kara) marks the starting point ("from").

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "I will wait until 5:00." (５時___待ちます。)
quizzes.explain: The particle "まで" (made) marks the ending point or limit ("until").

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "It takes 2 hours from Tokyo to Kyoto." (東京から京都___２時間かかります。)
quizzes.explain: The pair "から...まで" means "from... to...".

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "Mr. Yamada is a Japanese person." (山田さん___日本人です。)
quizzes.explain: The particle "は" (wa) marks the primary topic of the sentence.

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "Which one is your bag?" (どれ___あなたのカバンですか。)
quizzes.explain: Question words like どれ, だれ, なに must be followed by the subject marker "が" (ga), never "は".

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "Please write your name with a pen." (ペン___名前を書いてください。)
quizzes.explain: The particle "で" (de) indicates the tool or medium used to complete the action ("with a pen").

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "I bought three stamps." (切手を３枚___買いました。)
quizzes.explain: In Japanese, counters generally follow the object and the object-marker particle directly without an additional particle (切手を３枚買いました).

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "I will go to Kyoto on Sunday." (日曜日___京都へ行きます。)
quizzes.explain: Days of the week are specific time elements, so they take the particle "に" (ni) optionally or for emphasis.

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "There are two books on the desk." (机の上に本___２冊あります。)
quizzes.explain: The subject of existence with あります (to exist/have for inanimate objects) is marked with "が" (ga).

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "Tomorrow, will you go to the library too?" (明日、図書館___行きますか。)
quizzes.explain: To combine direction (へ) and addition (も), use the combined particle "へも" (he mo - "to ... also").

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "I met Mr. Tanaka." (田中さん___会いました。)
quizzes.explain: The verb 会う (au - to meet) takes the particle "に" (ni) to mark the person you meet.

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "I ride the bus." (バス___乗ります。)
quizzes.explain: The verb 乗る (noru - to ride/board a vehicle) takes the particle "に" (ni) to mark the vehicle.

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "I get off the train." (電車___降ります。)
quizzes.explain: The verb 降りる (oriru - to get off/exit a vehicle) takes the particle "を" (o) to mark the place of departure.

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "My house is far from the station." (わたしの家は駅___遠いです。)
quizzes.explain: The starting reference point for distance is marked by "から" (from).

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "This is a book about Japan." (これは日本___ついての本です。)
quizzes.explain: The compound pattern "~について" (ni tsuite) means "about / concerning".

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "This tea is very hot, isn't it?" (このお茶はとても熱いですね。)
quizzes.explain: The sentence-ending particle "ね" (ne) is used to seek agreement or confirm shared information ("isn't it?").

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "Japanese is very interesting, you know!" (日本語はとてもおもしろいですよ。)
quizzes.explain: The sentence-ending particle "よ" (yo) is used to assert new information or assure the listener ("you know / I tell you").

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "I read newspapers, magazines, etc." (新聞___雑誌などを読みます。)
quizzes.explain: The particle "や" (ya) is perfect for lists with "など" (nado - etc.).

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "I want a cup of hot water." (お湯___欲しいです。)
quizzes.explain: The adjective 欲しい (hoshii - want) requires the object to be marked with "が" (ga).

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "I went to Tokyo for travel." (旅行___東京へ行きました。)
quizzes.explain: The particle "で" (de) here indicates the purpose or reason/circumstance of the action.

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "I gave a flower to my mother." (母___花をあげました。)
quizzes.explain: The recipient of verbs of giving (あげる) is marked with the particle "に" (ni).

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "I received a present from my friend." (友達___プレゼントをもらいました。)
quizzes.explain: The source from whom you receive something (もらう) is marked with "から" (from) or "に" (by).

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "There are two cats under the table." (テーブルの下___ねこが２匹います。)
quizzes.explain: The particle "に" indicates the location of existence with います.

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "Please write here with a pencil." (鉛筆___書いてください。)
quizzes.explain: The tool/instrument (pencil) is marked with "で" (de).

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "Yesterday I bought bread and milk." (昨日パン___牛乳を買いました。)
quizzes.explain: The exhaustive particle "と" joins the two nouns.

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "Is there anyone in the room?" (部屋の中にだれ___いますか。)
quizzes.explain: "だれか" (dareka) means "someone" or "anyone".

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "No, there is no one." (いいえ、だれ___いません。)
quizzes.explain: "だれも" (daremo) paired with a negative verb means "no one".

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "I bought something at the supermarket." (スーパーで何か___買いました。)
quizzes.explain: "何か" (nanika - something) is treated as a self-contained unit and does not require the object marker particle "を".

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "Which one do you like?" (どれ___好きですか。)
quizzes.explain: Question words cannot be followed by は, they take the subject marker が.

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "I take a bath." (お風呂___入ります。)
quizzes.explain: The verb 入る (hairu - to enter/take a bath) takes the particle "に" (ni).

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "I bought this book at a bookstore." (本屋___この本を買いました。)
quizzes.explain: The location where the action of buying occurred is marked by "で" (de).

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "I am good at Japanese." (わたしは日本語___上手です。)
quizzes.explain: The descriptive adjective 上手 (jouzu - good at) takes the particle "が" (ga) to mark the subject/skill.

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "I am bad at English." (わたしは英語___下手です。)
quizzes.explain: The descriptive adjective 下手 (heta - bad at) takes the particle "が" (ga) to mark the subject/skill.

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "I will leave the office at 6:00." (６時___会社を出ます。)
quizzes.explain: Specific time points take "に" (ni).

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "I bought a nice camera." (いいカメラ___買いました。)
quizzes.explain: The direct object "カメラ" of "買いました" is marked by "を" (o).

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "My brother is a high school student." (兄___高校生です。)
quizzes.explain: The sentence topic is marked by "は" (wa).

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "Please give me that book." (その本___ください。)
quizzes.explain: The polite request "ください" takes the direct object marker "を" (o).

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "There are many flowers in the park." (公園に花___たくさんあります。)
quizzes.explain: The subject of existence with あります is marked with "が" (ga).

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "I played tennis with my brother." (弟___テニスをしました。)
quizzes.explain: The companion particle "と" indicates "with".

quizzes.q: What is the correct Japanese greeting for "Good Morning"?
quizzes.explain: "おはようございます" (Ohayou gozaimasu) is the polite greeting for good morning.

quizzes.q: What is the correct Japanese greeting for "Good Evening"?
quizzes.explain: "こんばんは" (Konbanwa) is the standard greeting for good evening.

quizzes.q: Which word means "Tomorrow" in Japanese?
quizzes.explain: "あした" (ashita) means tomorrow. きのう is yesterday, きょう is today.

quizzes.q: Which word means "Yesterday" in Japanese?
quizzes.explain: "きのう" (kinou) means yesterday.

quizzes.q: What is the Japanese word for "Family"?
quizzes.explain: "かぞく" (kazoku) means family.

quizzes.q: What does the word "あたたかい" (atatakai) mean?
quizzes.explain: "あたたかい" (atatakai) means warm (weather or object).

quizzes.q: What is the opposite of "高い" (takai - expensive/high)?
quizzes.explain: The opposite of expensive (高い) is cheap (安い - yasui).

quizzes.q: What is the Japanese counter for flat objects like paper and plates?
quizzes.explain: "~枚" (~mai) is the counter for flat, thin objects.

quizzes.q: What is the Japanese counter for books and notebooks?
quizzes.explain: "~冊" (~satsu) is the counter for bound items like books.

quizzes.q: What is the Japanese counter for long, cylindrical objects like pens and bottles?
quizzes.explain: "~本" (~hon/pon/bon) is the counter for long objects.

quizzes.q: What does "あぶない" (abunai) mean?
quizzes.explain: "あぶない" (abunai) means dangerous.

quizzes.q: Which of the following means "Apple" in Japanese?
quizzes.explain: "りんご" (ringo) means apple.

quizzes.q: What does the verb "おきる" (okiru) mean?
quizzes.explain: "おきる" (okiru) means to wake up or get up.

quizzes.q: What does the verb "ねる" (neru) mean?
quizzes.explain: "ねる" (neru) means to sleep or go to bed.

quizzes.q: What is the Japanese word for "Airplane"?
quizzes.explain: "飛行機" (ひこうき - hikouki) means airplane.

quizzes.q: What is the Japanese word for "Subway"?
